heading: Getting started / Opening CAPS
paragraph: Go to the App Menu, search for CAPS, and click on it to open the application. You will be directed to the CAPS interface.

heading: Getting started / Navigating CAPS interface
paragraph: Settings and About: Provides options for managing and configuring the application's connections to other services and instances.

heading: Importing climate data
paragraph: A dialog box will appear, prompting you to select a dataset template. Click the dropdown arrow to view the available climate dataset templates, then select the one you need. For example, Precipitation rate (CHIRPS3, monthly) (Monthly).

heading: Importing climate data
paragraph: The ingestion process will start immediately. A blue notification box will appear at the top of the interface, indicating that the ingestion process is running.

heading: Importing climate data
paragraph: Once the ingestion process is complete, a success message will appear. The newly imported dataset will then be available in the dataset list.

heading: Connecting to an instance
paragraph: Complete the form with the details of the instance you want to connect to.

heading: Connecting to an instance
paragraph: Choose an authentication method. You can connect using a Personal Access Token (recommended), which you must have already created in the source instance through the profile menu. Alternatively, you can use the username and password for the

heading: Connecting to an instance
paragraph: To view the connected instance, navigate to the About section. The instance will be displayed as a card showing its name, connection status, and other relevant details.

heading: Connecting to an instance
paragraph: To manage a connected instance, return to Settings. From there, you can edit its details, test the connection, or delete the connection.

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline / Pulling data from other instance

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline / Pulling data from other instance

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline / Pulling data from other instance

heading: Creating Pipelines / Creating a new pipeline / Pulling data from other instance

paragraph: The number in brackets is the count of schedules on this pipeline. The same convention applies to Steps, so a pipeline reading Steps (14) and Schedules (1) has fourteen steps and one schedule attached to them. A pipeline with no schedules s

paragraph: In the Schedules tab, click Add Schedule.

paragraph: 1. Identification

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / The cron expression
paragraph: The cron expression

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / Presets
paragraph: Every hour writes 0 * * * *. Minute 0 with every other unit unrestricted, so the pipeline runs at the top of every hour. The NEXT 3 RUNS panel shows three consecutive hours.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / Presets
paragraph: Daily 02:00 writes 0 2 * * *. Minute 0 of hour 2, every day, so the next three runs fall on consecutive dates at 02:00.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / Presets
paragraph: Weekly Mon restricts the weekday to 1, giving 0 2 * * 1 here. The next three runs are seven days apart.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / Presets
paragraph: Monthly 1st restricts the day of the month to 1 and releases the weekday, giving 0 2 1 * * here. The next three runs fall on the first of three consecutive months.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 2. Trigger / Confirming the timing before saving
paragraph: Two panels below the expression translate it back.

paragraph: Step's period

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 3. Input context / Period / Step's period
paragraph: “Latest periods: the last 3 complete months” means the step already holds a rolling window. Each run moves forward on its own, and no override is needed. This is the healthy case.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 3. Input context / Period / Latest periods
paragraph: Latest periods

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 3. Input context / Organisation units
paragraph: Beneath the period settings, each step offers an organisation unit override, introduced by the line Runs use the step's organisation units unless you choose others here.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 3. Input context / Organisation units
paragraph: Left unticked, the step runs against whatever organisation units it already holds. This is the usual state, and the block stays collapsed to a single line.

heading: Scheduling a pipeline / 3. Input context / Training period on prediction steps
paragraph: A step using the Prediction Trigger handler presents a training period in place of a data period. The training period is the span of past data the model learns from, which is a separate question from the span of data the pipeline fetches.
